description: The International Methane Emissions Observatory (IMEO) of the UN Environment Programme publishes methane data through its Eye on Methane data platform, both read on 2026-09-26. IMEO collects and synthesises data from its Methane Science Studies, from satellites through the Methane Alert and Response System (MARS), from company reporting under the Oil and Gas Methane Partnership 2.0 (OGMP 2.0), and from national inventories. The platform shows measured emissions from companies in OGMP 2.0, emissions from metallurgical coal mines, MARS-validated methane plumes on a world map across oil and gas, coal, waste and agriculture, and science studies, with a section for downloading open data sets. Companies and governments get dedicated secure spaces: governments review MARS alerts of high-volume emission events. New tools list the world's top 50 satellite-detected emitters and response rates to country alerts, and a Methane Emissions Index of regional oil and gas emissions was introduced in September 2026. Public data are free to view and download; the pages read state no licence beyond UNEP terms of use. Caveats: company data are self-reported and validated, and satellite detection favours large plumes. Simulation uses are locating leaking gas and oil assets for hazard exposure and resilience studies and validating emission estimates. Related records: data-viirs-nightfire-gas-flaring-eog maps gas flares from space.
